vexrath-042b63581cc3.speaker: vexrath
vexrath-042b63581cc3.text: Honour is earned. Today, we earned it.

nettle-e08e51e716e4.speaker: nettle
nettle-e08e51e716e4.text: I'll make this sound even better than it was.

osric-affd9c6db092.speaker: osric
osric-affd9c6db092.text: You carry shadows, child. Hold still... There. The Temple has lifted what clung to you.

rowan-28bc1f5e5324.speaker: rowan
rowan-28bc1f5e5324.text: Hale wrote to me. Said a stranger gave him back his courage. I'd wager that was you. The Watch owes you.

rowan-b5f631e39493.speaker: rowan
rowan-b5f631e39493.text: You brought Hale's name to me. Hard thing to do. I'll see he gets a fair hearing. Thank you.

rowan-7a2881144391.speaker: rowan
rowan-7a2881144391.text: Hale says someone leaned on him down there. I'm not saying it was you. I'm saying I noticed.

marga-956394797cb7.speaker: marga
marga-956394797cb7.text: Funny thing: the scratching under my cellar floor has gone quiet. Rats seem... respectful lately. Is that you? Don't answer.

marga-d79561240e96.speaker: marga
marga-d79561240e96.text: Something's been digging in my cellar all night. They're wearing tiny gold thimbles. Do you know anything about that?

osric-c68d059252f6.speaker: osric
osric-c68d059252f6.text: A drowned soul came to me in a dream, smiling. They say you paid his fare. The Temple blesses you.

osric-eabc82ffee02.speaker: osric
osric-eabc82ffee02.text: The dead keep accounts, child. I pray you balance yours.

wren-76f9a1b6edd1.speaker: wren
wren-76f9a1b6edd1.text: Tobble's back in town! He says you walked him out yourself. Dear heart, I'm making you a tea.

wren-50c08797b15d.speaker: wren
wren-50c08797b15d.text: Tobble says you fed him and let him keep his pride. That's worth more than glowcaps.

wren-ed445890b927.speaker: wren
wren-ed445890b927.text: Tobble came in with an empty pouch and a full heart of anger. I'm not saying anything. I'm saying a very loud nothing.

dobbin-639d0e781f2c.speaker: dobbin
dobbin-639d0e781f2c.text: One strike, they say. One clean strike. That's how it's done.

dobbin-1eec56807604.speaker: dobbin
dobbin-1eec56807604.text: Word is you struck the Silent Anvil twice. Show me your hands, lad. Hm. Steady. Good smithing in those.

dobbin-a7857ae2916b.speaker: dobbin
dobbin-a7857ae2916b.text: You left the old anvil alone. Smart. My grandfather struck it twice. Never did get the shaking out of his hands.

dobbin-a18a367b17a4.speaker: dobbin
dobbin-a18a367b17a4.text: My brothers say a foreman gave them water in the dark. Not forgiveness, mind. But I heard you let him walk. I'll think on it.

dobbin-dc1e3e09cf03.speaker: dobbin
dobbin-dc1e3e09cf03.text: They say the foreman never walked out of the Forge. My brothers were chained by him. I won't weep.

tamsin-63b824041f88.speaker: tamsin
tamsin-63b824041f88.text: Oh, pet. I heard the old horn in my sleep last night. Somebody swore the Warden's oath. Was that you?

tamsin-566f4c019736.speaker: tamsin
tamsin-566f4c019736.text: Somebody swore to guard each other in that vault, pet. Not the town, each other. That's the oath that holds.

tamsin-0cb5dfa8b84e.speaker: tamsin
tamsin-0cb5dfa8b84e.text: The old Warden's gauntlet is gone from the vault, I hear. Well. Everything is for sale in the end. Not everything, pet.

narrator-964b660b23fb.speaker: narrator
narrator-964b660b23fb.text: Sister Vey sinks beneath the water, her hymn ending in bubbles.

narrator-457c3bab8cab.speaker: narrator
narrator-457c3bab8cab.text: Mother Sporegrave collapses into a heap of harmless puffballs.

narrator-23a0f035fd03.speaker: narrator
narrator-23a0f035fd03.text: Skarn tumbles from the Broodmother's back. Among his things: Elowen's ribbon, and a map marked "B2".

narrator-ef47508ef713.speaker: narrator
narrator-ef47508ef713.text: Brambur pries his mother's hammer from Brakk's grip and weeps into his beard.

narrator-e1f5f624efeb.speaker: narrator
narrator-e1f5f624efeb.text: The moon rises over Emberhollow. A seal on the Blackspire cracks and breaks.

narrator-6ca6744a8b32.speaker: narrator
narrator-6ca6744a8b32.text: You cut a bound town guard free. "Captain Rowan sent you? Bless you!"

narrator-3d169bdf9141.speaker: narrator
narrator-3d169bdf9141.text: Lore tablet: "Emberhollow was founded on a sealed tower. The founders buried it, built an inn on top, and agreed never to mention it again."

narrator-f9ad28e4a124.speaker: narrator
narrator-f9ad28e4a124.text: Spoon clue 1: a spoon scratched into the wall, pointing down. "THE KEEPERS SLEEP BENEATH." Pip trembles with joy.

narrator-8dcbd1afd252.speaker: narrator
narrator-8dcbd1afd252.text: A fresh tunnel, dug straight up toward the Boar & Spoon cellar. You kick out the supports and it caves in. Marga will want to hear.

narrator-d5ae81864589.speaker: narrator
narrator-d5ae81864589.text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 1: "Down in the Warrens where the rat-kings sup, / Grumsh drew his axe and the rats gave up!"

narrator-b4df2862eaa3.speaker: narrator
narrator-b4df2862eaa3.text: Dwarven boot-prints, and a hammer-shaped dent in a rat. "That's Mum's hammer," Brambur whispers. "Someone took it deeper."

narrator-98803d339b3d.speaker: narrator
narrator-98803d339b3d.text: The ceiling here sags over a side-passage where you hear cultists chanting. One good pull would bring it down on them, or on you.

narrator-a8d358051ef2.speaker: narrator
narrator-a8d358051ef2.text: CRACK! The ceiling caves in on the cultist side-passage. Silence, and a pouch of 40 gp rolls out of the dust.

narrator-031e4c35a1b3.speaker: narrator
narrator-031e4c35a1b3.text: A torn spellbook page, covered in Fizzwick's tiny handwriting ("NOTE TO SELF: COUNTERSPELL. ALWAYS COUNTERSPELL.").

narrator-7143cc5e89d0.speaker: narrator
narrator-7143cc5e89d0.text: Spoon clue 2: a tarnished teaspoon tied to a stalactite with a ribbon marked "II". Pip pockets it reverently.

narrator-85af568041e5.speaker: narrator
narrator-85af568041e5.text: Half-sunk in the grotto: a satchel stitched with the royal sun. Elowen's temple relics, still dry inside. Brother Osric will want this.

narrator-cee2db010071.speaker: narrator
narrator-cee2db010071.text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 2: "In the Grotto deep where the waters sing, / a lizard with a club tail met a better thing!"

narrator-63269c9ce4eb.speaker: narrator
narrator-63269c9ce4eb.text: Tall tale 1: "The staff was carved from a lightning-struck spire," Nettle writes. "Everyone agrees. Nobody saw it."

narrator-7702f63d140e.speaker: narrator
narrator-7702f63d140e.text: Lore tablet: "The First Warden bound the Tyrant-lizard Gorvax beneath the vault with five seals and a very large horn."

narrator-d407f7b1366b.speaker: narrator
narrator-d407f7b1366b.text: You shatter a humming crystal pylon. Stored dawn-light spills out and sinks into the floor, heading deeper.

narrator-8b54b3b2962d.speaker: narrator
narrator-8b54b3b2962d.text: Spoon clue 3: crystal etchings of five spoons in a circle. One is a ladle. "That's cheating," says Pip.

narrator-1ca03ad5e1ec.speaker: narrator
narrator-1ca03ad5e1ec.text: A crystal-sealed royal decree. The ORIGINAL. It does not exile Vexrath's clan; it knights them.

narrator-68582edc7c66.speaker: narrator
narrator-68582edc7c66.text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 3: "Through Glimmerdeep's glow where the toadstools scream, / Grumsh screamed louder (it was quite the scene)!"

narrator-09d9696f6da0.speaker: narrator
narrator-09d9696f6da0.text: Tall tale 2: "It hums when he lies," Nettle notes. "So it hums constantly."

narrator-be74ef149940.speaker: narrator
narrator-be74ef149940.text: Lore tablet: "Glimmerdeep crystals drink light. Shatter them and the light they hoarded is set free."

narrator-4f15dbe8682f.speaker: narrator
narrator-4f15dbe8682f.text: You smash the chains of a captive smith. "Tell Dobbin we're coming home, and we'll be at the vault when you need us."

narrator-a98dacac81e9.speaker: narrator
narrator-a98dacac81e9.text: A keg of dwarven blasting powder. Zizzy's eyes light up. "Oh, we are SO using this on the gate."

narrator-bc880204ffdd.speaker: narrator
narrator-bc880204ffdd.text: A keg of dwarven blasting powder. It looks like the sort of thing a sorcerer would enjoy.

narrator-dba52dde8de1.speaker: narrator
narrator-dba52dde8de1.text: Spoon clue 4: an anvil stamped with a spoon. Under it, a riddle: "Where the Tyrant sleeps, the silver keeps."

narrator-544500ad8657.speaker: narrator
narrator-544500ad8657.text: Zizzy packs the powder against the Ashforge gate. KA-BOOM! The gate, and its guards, are no longer a problem.

narrator-d078d1313e77.speaker: narrator
narrator-d078d1313e77.text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 4: "In Ashforge's heat where the anvils ring, / Grumsh rang louder, being Grumsh, the king!"

narrator-d2121f25121b.speaker: narrator
narrator-d2121f25121b.text: Tall tale 3: "A smith says the staff has a crack near the crystal, mended with cultist spit."

narrator-9fec26629db9.speaker: narrator
narrator-9fec26629db9.text: Lore tablet: "Ashforge was a dwarven forge-hall until Brakk sold it, and its smiths, to the Sovereign."

narrator-fdc59d7476b3.speaker: narrator
narrator-fdc59d7476b3.text: Old Tamsin's tale was true. You will sound it when the Tyrant rises.

narrator-3a43f3eb8f0e.speaker: narrator
narrator-3a43f3eb8f0e.text: Spoon clue 5: the final clue, a spoon-shaped keyhole in the vault wall. Pip hums the Spoon-Keepers' anthem.

narrator-f69e01572ceb.speaker: narrator
narrator-f69e01572ceb.text: A drunken carving on the wall inspires Grumsh. Verse 5: "In the Blackspire vault where the Tyrant lay, / [Grumsh: 'Last line comes after we win.']"

narrator-e31ededc2560.speaker: narrator
narrator-e31ededc2560.text: Tall tale 4: "There it is: the crack is under the third ring. Strike there and the whole thing goes." Nettle underlines it twice.

narrator-cb51d2123401.speaker: narrator
narrator-cb51d2123401.text: Pip fits the five clues into a spoon-shaped keyhole. A wall slides away: the SECRET ARMORY of the Spoon-Keepers!

narrator-63d474e31255.speaker: narrator
narrator-63d474e31255.text: Lore tablet: "MALTHRAX. Once court wizard of Emberhollow. Exiled for 'excessive candlelight'. Took it personally."

narrator-d14fe5c055b0.speaker: narrator
narrator-d14fe5c055b0.text: Thimbles, buttons and a wedge of cheese the size of a wagon wheel ring a painted rat in a tiny crown. The rats around it have gone very quiet. All of them are looking at you.

narrator-a444406f20fc.speaker: narrator
narrator-a444406f20fc.text: The thimbles are heavy, bright gold. Somewhere inside the walls, a thousand tiny feet start moving.

narrator-ae1979452ae5.speaker: narrator
narrator-ae1979452ae5.text: You set a coin before the crown. The rats bow. Truly. The tunnels feel quieter.

narrator-f3845bbaa402.speaker: narrator
narrator-f3845bbaa402.text: It is alarmingly good cheese. Pip is moved to tears. Everyone feels rested and oddly proud.

narrator-b63b65c74f84.speaker: narrator
narrator-b63b65c74f84.text: A guardsman in a scorched Watch tabard sits wedged in a niche, sword across his knees. "Corporal Hale," he mumbles. "I ran. When the cultists came, I ran. I can't go back to the Captain. I can't."

narrator-5c946cfbd148.speaker: narrator
narrator-5c946cfbd148.text: "Thank you. I'll tell Rowan myself." He straightens a little, tabard and all. You feel like you did something that matters.

narrator-9e1ea6c307c8.speaker: narrator
narrator-9e1ea6c307c8.text: He closes his eyes and nods. "Fair." You note his name and leave him his sword. Duty is a heavy coat.

narrator-783d1f1e2310.speaker: narrator
narrator-783d1f1e2310.text: He hands over a battered pouch without meeting your eyes. It stings a little, taking it.

narrator-57e949c96bdf.speaker: narrator
narrator-57e949c96bdf.text: A bronze bell hangs half-sunk in a black pool, its rope trailing underwater. It tolls once, very softly, though nothing touched it.

narrator-cf7c3c554cb6.speaker: narrator
narrator-cf7c3c554cb6.text: Each toll rolls out across the water. Something far away answers, then thinks better of it. You feel rather wiser, and rather watched.

narrator-4602e73b5ac2.speaker: narrator
narrator-4602e73b5ac2.text: Cold hands find a clapper of pearl-white bone-metal. It hums in your palm: a fortune charm, still warm.

narrator-b5287295d618.speaker: narrator
narrator-b5287295d618.text: The water is deeper than it looks. You scramble out, coughing, with nothing but a bruise and a lesson.

narrator-86fae8805258.speaker: narrator
narrator-86fae8805258.text: The bell sighs out one last quiet note, as if relieved. Brambur prays for it.

narrator-033d4b235109.speaker: narrator
narrator-033d4b235109.text: A drowned ferryman sits in a rotted skiff, one dripping hand held out. "Thirty years I have waited for a fare," he says. "Pay, and I may finally sleep."

narrator-69172414a384.speaker: narrator
narrator-69172414a384.text: He bows. The skiff slides gently under the black water, and in the ripples lies a pearl the size of a plum.

narrator-dd4bf1c99b90.speaker: narrator
narrator-dd4bf1c99b90.text: The words come true and quiet. He sighs, smiles, and the skiff goes down with him. The tunnels feel safer.

narrator-04ecab46717e.speaker: narrator
narrator-04ecab46717e.text: He listens to the whole prayer, kindly. "A good try," he says. "I will wait a little longer." He gives you a nod.

narrator-e2505dbb5463.speaker: narrator
narrator-e2505dbb5463.text: You find a cache of waterlogged coins. The ferryman watches you without a word. It is somehow the worst part.

narrator-e679e3912e9e.speaker: narrator
narrator-e679e3912e9e.text: A tall crystal shows each of you as you truly are: braver, kinder and a little more frightened than you thought. It hums, waiting.

narrator-d120d2f804c6.speaker: narrator
narrator-d120d2f804c6.text: You each see what you are. Nobody speaks for a while, but everyone feels clearer. A strange new steadiness settles over the party.

narrator-69944d6965e1.speaker: narrator
narrator-69944d6965e1.text: The shards are worth a small fortune. The purse in your pocket feels suspiciously lighter afterwards.

narrator-dc886e55bc1c.speaker: narrator
narrator-dc886e55bc1c.text: The facets are tuned like a harp. You find a seam, and a small lens of mirror-glass comes away in your hand.

narrator-6834d5076e2d.speaker: narrator
narrator-6834d5076e2d.text: The crystal gives you a headache, and a very smug reflection of yourself. That is all.

narrator-2657638dbce0.speaker: narrator
narrator-2657638dbce0.text: A gnome with a lantern for a hat huddles in a crystal seam, sobbing into a pouch of glowing mushrooms. "Tobble Grindlewick!" he sniffles. "I sell glowcaps to the herbalist in Emberhollow! I got lost three days ago!"

narrator-437d34b55b98.speaker: narrator
narrator-437d34b55b98.text: It takes a while, and a little shouting. Tobble hugs your boots and runs for the surface. You feel good about it.

narrator-6418ae6cacf3.speaker: narrator
narrator-6418ae6cacf3.text: He eats everything, thanks you with enormous dignity, and gives you a bundle of the best glowcaps. "For the herbalist. Or you."

narrator-1cfa2a4ceeb3.speaker: narrator
narrator-1cfa2a4ceeb3.text: It is heavy and bright. He does not stop you. You realise a bit late that he is looking at you as if you were a monster.

narrator-7b7c4956ffc3.speaker: narrator
narrator-7b7c4956ffc3.text: An anvil older than the Forge stands in a ring of cold ash, a hammer laid across its face. Words are cut into the iron: STRIKE ONCE FOR STRENGTH. STRIKE TWICE FOR FEAR.

narrator-ed9868da6eeb.speaker: narrator
narrator-ed9868da6eeb.text: A single clear note rings out of the iron. Your hands steady, and the next chest you open will feel lucky.

narrator-c48ad6156c92.speaker: narrator
narrator-c48ad6156c92.text: The second ring is wrong: deep and hungry. It gives you something precious and takes something less visible. The dead stir in the walls.

narrator-8bde43e09553.speaker: narrator
narrator-8bde43e09553.text: You lay the hammer neatly across the anvil. A faint warmth follows you: respect, from something old. A flask of tempering oil appears at your feet.

narrator-57544376a96c.speaker: narrator
narrator-57544376a96c.text: A burned cultist foreman kneels beside a cooling channel, sobbing. "Mercy. I only held the keys. I never struck them. Let me go, and I will tell you where the smiths are held."

narrator-8988a7a90949.speaker: narrator
narrator-8988a7a90949.text: He gives you the keys and a hurried map of the lower forges. He bolts for the stairs, and a quiet nod from the party says you were right.

narrator-15e9b8004f7e.speaker: narrator
narrator-15e9b8004f7e.text: He swears on his mother, his mother's mother and the keys. He leaves, and you leave with his purse.

narrator-641769690226.speaker: narrator
narrator-641769690226.text: He laughs, hysterical, and darts away into the dark. The keys remain, but his promise does not.

narrator-e2c99e753735.speaker: narrator
narrator-e2c99e753735.text: It is quick and ugly. His keys are good keys, and his purse is heavy. Nobody says anything for a while.

narrator-7c72453111a0.speaker: narrator
narrator-7c72453111a0.text: A weathered statue of a Warden stands with open hands. At its feet a cracked plate reads: WHO KEEPS THE SEALS KEEPS THE TOWN. A faint horn-note hangs in the air.

narrator-a95d7310e88b.speaker: narrator
narrator-a95d7310e88b.text: The statue's hands close, just slightly, around yours. Warmth floods the party, and the hush of a good road settles around you.

narrator-6b245607b470.speaker: narrator
narrator-6b245607b470.text: Four voices, one oath. The statue's head tilts, almost fondly. The bond of the party tightens.

narrator-d15f539c0ef7.speaker: narrator
narrator-d15f539c0ef7.text: It comes away with a groan of old iron. Even as you lift it, you know the vault is going to remember this.

narrator-bb9e0f1affb3.speaker: narrator
narrator-bb9e0f1affb3.text: A cracked seal in the wall breathes a voice like warm oil. "Little knights. I can make you stronger. I ask only for a small favour."

narrator-937ed955c827.speaker: narrator
narrator-937ed955c827.text: Power pours into your hand. Something cold settles into your purse, and the dead begin to turn in their sleep.

narrator-d0e80565330c.speaker: narrator
narrator-d0e80565330c.text: The seal sputters, outraged. Nerves steady across the party, and the vault seems to wince.

narrator-b8e2b5e8f569.speaker: narrator
narrator-b8e2b5e8f569.text: Scratched into the wall: "SKARN RIDES THE SPIDER QUEEN. THE RUSTY KEY OPENS HER DEN."

narrator-527ffbd1e728.speaker: narrator
narrator-527ffbd1e728.text: A faded mural shows a lizard as big as a cathedral. Someone has drawn a mustache on it.

narrator-57225b0cefe4.speaker: narrator
narrator-57225b0cefe4.text: A note: "Pip was here. Took spoon. Not sorry."

narrator-0ab37f479651.speaker: narrator
narrator-0ab37f479651.text: Dripping water spells nothing in particular. Brambur apologizes to it anyway.

narrator-85883228ce39.speaker: narrator
narrator-85883228ce39.text: An inscription: "BEYOND THE CORAL DOOR SLEEPS OLD CLUBTAIL. BRING SNACKS."

narrator-d6e67426a1bb.speaker: narrator
narrator-d6e67426a1bb.text: A cracked mirror. Professor Fizzwick spends some time admiring it.

narrator-ccf374b26192.speaker: narrator
narrator-ccf374b26192.text: The crystals here show your reflection a half-second late. Fizzwick waves at his. It waves back early.

narrator-14d0ffd63442.speaker: narrator
narrator-14d0ffd63442.text: Scratched in a crystal: "DO NOT LOOK THE LIZARD IN THE EYE. USE A MIRROR. a statue, probably"

narrator-964677ae5c65.speaker: narrator
narrator-964677ae5c65.text: A circle of mushrooms. Grumsh steps in it and refuses to say what he saw.

narrator-75d75fc1ae12.speaker: narrator
narrator-75d75fc1ae12.text: An anvil, still warm, with a smith's name scratched on it: "VARR".

narrator-3713fc56ea26.speaker: narrator
narrator-3713fc56ea26.text: A forge-mural: dwarves, a chimera, and a very small Brakk hiding behind it.

narrator-730bd18f9b7e.speaker: narrator
narrator-730bd18f9b7e.text: A sign: "BRAKK'S FORGE. NO REFUNDS. NO DWARVES. NO CHIMERA-PETTING."

narrator-20b6802e4a33.speaker: narrator
narrator-20b6802e4a33.text: Carved in gold: "HE WHO TAKES THE DAWNSTONE AMULET SHALL HOLD THE FIVE SEALS."

narrator-de7856d9d686.speaker: narrator
narrator-de7856d9d686.text: Enormous footprints. Fizzwick measures one. "Fizzwick estimates: large."

narrator-1823753fe18e.speaker: narrator
narrator-1823753fe18e.text: A shrine to a forgotten god of cutlery. Pip weeps openly.

narrator-58c024482a81.speaker: narrator
narrator-58c024482a81.text: Scratched into the stone: "The wardens fed the rats first, so the rats would learn to love the dark. They did."

narrator-b8906c2669ea.speaker: narrator
narrator-b8906c2669ea.text: A child's tally of days, 41 marks, then a drawing of a door.

narrator-c1925c67caf2.speaker: narrator
narrator-c1925c67caf2.text: A drowned scribe left a note: "The water was never a flood. It was a door the Tyrant wanted shut."

narrator-139a53db5dfa.speaker: narrator
narrator-139a53db5dfa.text: Pressed flowers, long dried: someone kept a garden down here.

narrator-05594a4b6f9b.speaker: narrator
narrator-05594a4b6f9b.text: Crystal-etched verse: "Glass remembers every face that looked into it. Do not look long."

narrator-6b41bd1bc0c1.speaker: narrator
narrator-6b41bd1bc0c1.text: A map fragment with a single mark: "The Warden sleeps standing."

narrator-46effa2a4319.speaker: narrator
narrator-46effa2a4319.text: Forge-script: "Every blade of Ashforge was quenched in a prisoner's name. Brakk kept the list."

narrator-4cc85d731a08.speaker: narrator
narrator-4cc85d731a08.text: A small hammer, wrapped in cloth. No name on it.

narrator-2829e31de58c.speaker: narrator
narrator-2829e31de58c.text: Carved over the lintel: "Gorvax was not the first thing to rule here. He is simply the loudest."

narrator-a95eb0f97eaf.speaker: narrator
narrator-a95eb0f97eaf.text: A saddle-strap, thunder-lizard hide. Someone rode these once.

narrator-d4d80f58f92c.speaker: narrator
narrator-d4d80f58f92c.text: The camp is quiet. Too quiet.

narrator-3ed82cf32abb.speaker: narrator
narrator-3ed82cf32abb.text: Back in the Rat-Warrens. The scratching starts up again.

narrator-f5c72615823b.speaker: narrator
narrator-f5c72615823b.text: The Drowned Grotto. Cold water closes over your boots once more.

narrator-27beacd47762.speaker: narrator
narrator-27beacd47762.text: The Glimmerdeep hums its single note. Your reflections are waiting.

narrator-92bfd56cf939.speaker: narrator
narrator-92bfd56cf939.text: The Ashforge heat greets you like an old, bad-tempered friend.

narrator-be06dc8a2a14.speaker: narrator
narrator-be06dc8a2a14.text: The Vault. The breathing has not stopped.

narrator-00a876dd1952.speaker: narrator
narrator-00a876dd1952.text: Here the rat-sign stops, as if even the vermin give this spot a wide berth. Something waits here that is not a rat.

narrator-fdeddfde6919.speaker: narrator
narrator-fdeddfde6919.text: Clear water bubbles from a cracked basin carved with a smiling face. It smells, astonishingly, of mint.

narrator-b4d1c4c33c02.speaker: narrator
narrator-b4d1c4c33c02.text: A spiral stair corkscrews down into the dark. A cold draught rises from it, carrying the smell of standing water.

narrator-e7b40c694e6a.speaker: narrator
narrator-e7b40c694e6a.text: The hidden passage is lined with tiny claw-marked tallies. Someone, or several someones, has been counting days here.

narrator-327b80946f51.speaker: narrator
narrator-327b80946f51.text: A low chamber stacked with mouldy grain sacks, every one of them gnawed open. The floor crunches underfoot, and you decide not to look down.

narrator-38bcddf484fc.speaker: narrator
narrator-38bcddf484fc.text: Dozens of tiny shrines line this room: thimbles, buttons and bent spoons arranged with real devotion around a portrait of a very fat rat.

narrator-8d398a0537ca.speaker: narrator
narrator-8d398a0537ca.text: Water pools in the middle of this chamber, and the walls are furred with nests of shredded cloth. The smell is magnificent, in the worst way.

narrator-d9f30bfe51c0.speaker: narrator
narrator-d9f30bfe51c0.text: Old smuggler's crates rot in the corners, stamped with the crest of Emberhollow. One still rattles faintly when you pass.

narrator-9d6badccf754.speaker: narrator
narrator-9d6badccf754.text: A ring of half-sunken lanterns marks this place, each one still somehow burning beneath the water.

narrator-ed9ae9d40880.speaker: narrator
narrator-ed9ae9d40880.text: A spring of warm, glowing water rises here, fizzing gently. The fungus around it grows in the shape of open hands.

narrator-e09c7b2b93d5.speaker: narrator
narrator-e09c7b2b93d5.text: Steps slick with algae lead down past a waterline carved with the warning "HIGH TIDE". The ink is fresh.

narrator-8a9ebb9efd23.speaker: narrator
narrator-8a9ebb9efd23.text: Behind the false wall is a dry pocket of air that smells of old parchment. Someone hid here while the water rose.

narrator-0569952d3f06.speaker: narrator
narrator-0569952d3f06.text: A flooded hall where bioluminescent eels drift between broken columns, lighting the water in slow blue pulses.

narrator-8e51f5cf02f0.speaker: narrator
narrator-8e51f5cf02f0.text: Shipwreck timbers jut from the walls of this cave, though the sea is miles away. A barnacled figurehead watches you pass.

narrator-c7450fdaf8aa.speaker: narrator
narrator-c7450fdaf8aa.text: Stalactites drip in this grotto like a broken water clock. The pools below are full of tiny white crabs that click in unison.

narrator-9a1ea6db9271.speaker: narrator
narrator-9a1ea6db9271.text: Nets heavy with old catches hang from the ceiling here. Some of the catches are wearing boots.

narrator-75f9ddc8e0b8.speaker: narrator
narrator-75f9ddc8e0b8.text: The hum of the crystals drops to a low, almost-words murmur here, as if the cavern is trying to tell you something.

narrator-ae00794a10da.speaker: narrator
narrator-ae00794a10da.text: A pool of liquid starlight shimmers in a crystal bowl. Drinking it tastes like the first cold breath of winter.

narrator-7de588c09d6b.speaker: narrator
narrator-7de588c09d6b.text: A crystal stair spirals downward, each step chiming a note as you test it. The tune is not a happy one.

narrator-22e454f641f3.speaker: narrator
narrator-22e454f641f3.text: The concealed grotto is dark: no crystals, no reflections, no hum. The silence is the loudest thing you have heard all day.

narrator-bc62f88d53d3.speaker: narrator
narrator-bc62f88d53d3.text: A gallery of statues frozen mid-stride, each one carrying a mirror that was raised a moment too late.

narrator-369fdb67673f.speaker: narrator
narrator-369fdb67673f.text: Huge amethyst columns split the light into slow purple rainbows. The floor is warm, and faintly ticks like cooling glass.

narrator-ac3d17dd266b.speaker: narrator
narrator-ac3d17dd266b.text: A garden of luminous mushrooms grows in a perfect spiral here. Stepping off the path makes them all turn to face you.

narrator-e000cba1c7c8.speaker: narrator
narrator-e000cba1c7c8.text: Shards of a shattered geode the size of a cottage litter this chamber, still humming with whatever broke out of it.

narrator-0e20c41ef8de.speaker: narrator
narrator-0e20c41ef8de.text: Here the hammer-song stops. Tools lie where they were dropped, mid-swing, and the air smells of a hasty departure.

narrator-449c0988ab03.speaker: narrator
narrator-449c0988ab03.text: Cool water pours from the mouth of a stone dwarf into a quenching trough. Steam curls up, smelling of iron and relief.

narrator-53ab77840203.speaker: narrator
narrator-53ab77840203.text: A brass-railed stair plunges into dark heat. Each step down is a little warmer, and the walls start to sweat.

narrator-02eb08231bba.speaker: narrator
narrator-02eb08231bba.text: A hidden smithy, its tools neatly hung and its coals banked as if the smith stepped out for lunch a hundred years ago.

narrator-e63192e04923.speaker: narrator
narrator-e63192e04923.text: A chamber of cooling moulds, each one shaped like a different weapon. Several of the moulds are empty and still warm.

narrator-f32bc1223e42.speaker: narrator
narrator-f32bc1223e42.text: Bellows the size of houses wheeze in this hall, pushed by nothing you can see. Embers dance in the draught.

narrator-9dc1240b2637.speaker: narrator
narrator-9dc1240b2637.text: An ore-cart track loops through this cavern, and a cart full of glowing slag still creaks slowly along it.

narrator-93c7575fa67e.speaker: narrator
narrator-93c7575fa67e.text: Racks of half-finished armour line the walls here, helmets turned so that every empty visor watches the door.

narrator-4f41071a3f73.speaker: narrator
narrator-4f41071a3f73.text: Old murals here show tiny heroes fleeing a towering lizard. The last panel has been scratched out with claws.

narrator-9bc1cef621ce.speaker: narrator
narrator-9bc1cef621ce.text: A basin of violet light pulses slowly, like a resting heartbeat. The pain of the road drains away as you drink.

narrator-87cdec04142e.speaker: narrator
narrator-87cdec04142e.text: Elowen's light pours from the altar ahead, golden and steady. Five keyholes wait around its rim.

narrator-c9384da7cdcf.speaker: narrator
narrator-c9384da7cdcf.text: This hidden alcove holds the bones of a knight in mirrored armour, one hand still pointing toward the vault.

narrator-a77256f6cb40.speaker: narrator
narrator-a77256f6cb40.text: Eggshells as big as barrels lie cracked open across this chamber. Whatever hatched has had a long time to grow.

narrator-73bd2dd724d8.speaker: narrator
narrator-73bd2dd724d8.text: Carved pillars of roaring lizards hold up a ceiling lost in darkness. Rain-sound echoes from far above, though there is no sky.

narrator-639a646642ca.speaker: narrator
narrator-639a646642ca.text: A trophy hall of crushed shields and bent swords, each tagged with a name in neat, patient handwriting.

narrator-8bba228827e7.speaker: narrator
narrator-8bba228827e7.text: The floor here is scorched in a long, perfect line, as if lightning once ran along it on four legs.

narrator-dec8958b1c1e.speaker: narrator
narrator-dec8958b1c1e.text: Emberhollow huddles in the long shadow of the Blackspire, a jumble of slate roofs and leaning chimneys. The square smells of woodsmoke and hot pies, and a bell tolls the hour a little nervously. Townsfolk hurry past, glancing at the dark tower the way you glance at a sleeping dog. Everyone here has lost someone to the maze.

narrator-8f8a670b8d08.speaker: narrator
narrator-8f8a670b8d08.text: The Boar & Spoon is warm, loud and smells of spilled ale, roast onions and wet dog. A fiddler saws at something cheerful in the corner while a mounted boar's head, wearing a spoon on a string, watches the door. Adventurers swap tall tales at long tables, and every one of them has a story about the Blackspire.

narrator-28f49355f55e.speaker: narrator
narrator-28f49355f55e.text: The Temple of Cant is cool and hushed, lit by tall candles that never quite drip. Incense of cedar and myrrh drifts past a donation box the size of a coffin. Somewhere a priest is counting coins very quietly.

narrator-8bd3cbc0ad78.speaker: narrator
narrator-8bd3cbc0ad78.text: Straw dummies hang from posts in the Training Grounds, most of them missing their heads. The air rings with clashing steel, barked orders and the thud of arrows striking targets. A grizzled sergeant watches you sideways and mutters something about soft hands.

narrator-ae9bdf17af22.speaker: narrator
narrator-ae9bdf17af22.text: Fizzbang's Trading Post is an avalanche of goods waiting to happen: ropes, lanterns, potions and at least one suspicious barrel. It smells of lamp oil and lavender soap. A gnome peers at you over a counter piled high with "bargains".

narrator-a0714f6b37db.speaker: narrator
narrator-a0714f6b37db.text: The cobbles end at a ring of standing stones around a gaping stair. Cold air breathes up from below, carrying faint echoes: a drip, a scratch, something like distant laughter. The town's last lantern swings above the entrance, and nobody has ever bothered to light it.

serAldric-7729ab2e175a.text: Rise, friend. We are not done.

serAldric-6c127202c27a.text: I feel the Dawn grow stronger.

serAldric-9c06165475f8.speaker: serAldric

vp_gruffwarrior-e4d79f63f205.speaker: vp_gruffwarrior

vp_youngheroine-e607544b9b53.speaker: vp_youngheroine
vp_youngheroine-e607544b9b53.text: I am fine, I am fine!

vp_youngheroine-19c24007ff3e.speaker: vp_youngheroine
vp_youngheroine-19c24007ff3e.text: We did it! We really did it!

vp_youngheroine-dfd78d9ef616.speaker: vp_youngheroine
vp_youngheroine-dfd78d9ef616.text: Can we tell stories by the fire?

vp_wiseelder-ee939f5348a3.speaker: vp_wiseelder
vp_wiseelder-ee939f5348a3.text: Sit. Let me tell you a story.

vp_wiseelder-2099cfe37782.speaker: vp_wiseelder
vp_wiseelder-2099cfe37782.text: Ah, you have need of me?

vp_nobleknight-9f4185e76409.speaker: vp_nobleknight
vp_nobleknight-9f4185e76409.text: In the name of the Crown!

vp_nobleknight-df47c706efa6.speaker: vp_nobleknight
vp_nobleknight-df47c706efa6.text: A blow worthy of a song!

vp_nobleknight-aeea520143c9.speaker: vp_nobleknight
vp_nobleknight-aeea520143c9.text: I am worthy of the oath.

vp_nobleknight-e1540dc307a2.speaker: vp_nobleknight
vp_nobleknight-e1540dc307a2.text: I will stand to the last.

vp_cheerfulbard-ffad21eee31f.speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
vp_cheerfulbard-ffad21eee31f.text: And a one, and a two!

vp_cheerfulbard-9d76a38d6d2a.speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
vp_cheerfulbard-9d76a38d6d2a.text: Ooh, that is a sour note.

vp_cheerfulbard-25147bbf4dda.speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
vp_cheerfulbard-25147bbf4dda.text: That is a ballad, right there!

vp_cheerfulbard-e8dd14179f28.speaker: vp_cheerfulbard
vp_cheerfulbard-e8dd14179f28.text: No no no, not the finale!

vp_dourdwarf-fbb94a1efa70.speaker: vp_dourdwarf
vp_dourdwarf-fbb94a1efa70.text: I have had worse. Not much worse.

vp_dourdwarf-abf023e12f1a.speaker: vp_dourdwarf
vp_dourdwarf-abf023e12f1a.text: I do not like magic. Fine.

vp_dourdwarf-7297b80d1dfe.speaker: vp_dourdwarf
vp_dourdwarf-7297b80d1dfe.text: I knew it. I knew it.

vp_boomingbarbarian-b03146c62952.speaker: vp_boomingbarbarian
